title: SEO page brief or draft (AI-search era)

gates.text: Truth: no statistic, market price, case study, author credential, review or competitor claim that isn't in confirmed facts or cited research. Gaps are written around (pick an angle the confirmed facts fully support); never an invention, never a placeholder in publishable copy.
Spam policy: not a scaled or templated page (no city-swap, doorway or near-duplicate location pages); passes the city-swap test; no keyword stuffing or hidden text.

Format: title ≈ 50–60 characters, meta description ≈ 150–160 characters, one H1, a short slug, a named author (the business or its owner when no writer is confirmed), and schema limited to visible content with no self-serving review markup.

anchors.1: Wrong page type for the query (e.g. a blog essay for a transactional query).
anchors.5: Exactly the format the SERP rewards, chosen from a stated SERP read, and executed better than what ranks.
Own data, prices, photos, worked examples or experience no competing page has, placed early.

anchors.1: Answers buried after preamble; headings are vague.
anchors.3: Intro answers the query; some H2s bury their answers or sub-questions are missing.
anchors.5: Intro answers in 1–2 sentences; every H2 is a real sub-question answered in its first sentence; 5–10 fan-out questions covered.

anchors.3: Author named; sources or dates missing.
anchors.5: Named author with relevant experience, last-reviewed date, sourced external figures, original photos, contact and business details consistent with the Business Profile.

anchors.1: No internal links, or the page competes with an existing page.
anchors.3: A few links with generic anchors.
anchors.5: Up, across and down links plus 2–3 inbound links with descriptive anchors, inside a tight cluster around what the business sells.

anchors.1: Stuffed, truncated or generic title and meta.
anchors.5: Query words near the front in natural order; meta answers and gives a reason to click; opening paragraph quotable if Google rewrites.

anchors.1: Ignores AI features or recommends gimmicks (special AI files or schema).
anchors.3: Mentions AI Overviews without specific actions.
anchors.5: Snippet-eligible, quotable factual sentences, consistent facts across site and profiles, fan-out coverage, prompt-check and AI-referral tracking recommended.

anchors.1: No next step, or several competing CTAs.
anchors.5: One CTA that fits the intent, linked to the money page.

anchors.1: AI tells, throat-clearing intro, hedging filler.
anchors.5: Plain, specific, expert voice; tables and lists where they help; no filler.
